eyebrow: SQL Server Performance Tuning · Chapter Five
subtitle: Lesson 25 · Wait Statistics & Bottleneck Analysis

code:
SELECT wait_type, waiting_tasks_count,
       wait_time_ms, signal_wait_time_ms
FROM sys.dm_os_wait_stats
WHERE wait_type = 'SOS_SCHEDULER_YIELD';

-- corroborate with:
SELECT scheduler_id, runnable_tasks_count
FROM sys.dm_os_schedulers
WHERE status = 'VISIBLE ONLINE';
caption: Yielding the CPU because others are waiting for the scheduler.

code:
Parallel threads synchronizing
  = normal, expected wait

Worth chasing only when paired with:
  - thread SKEW (uneven per-thread
    row counts in the actual plan)
  - small OLTP queries going
    parallel unnecessarily
caption: A lot of parallel plans is not the same as a problem.

eyebrow: Which queries are actually spending the CPU
code:
SELECT TOP 20
    qs.total_worker_time / qs.execution_count
        AS avg_cpu_per_exec_us,
    qs.total_worker_time AS total_cpu_us,
    qs.execution_count
FROM sys.dm_exec_query_stats AS qs
ORDER BY qs.total_worker_time DESC;
caption: Sorted by CPU time, not duration — duration can just be waiting.
